# 📊 NBFC Daily Watch — Monday, November 23, 2026

Monday edition for 23 November 2026 (IST), covering Sunday 22 Nov to Monday morning. The NSE and BSE open at 09:15 today, so every stock and index figure is Friday 20 Nov's close; IBJA has not posted a 23 Nov rate yet, so the gold rows are the 20 Nov PM session; AGLOC's block is dated 23 Nov and applies today.

## 🔴 URGENT / High Impact

### RBI meets chief executives of top-tier NBFCs today; no agenda has been published
The Reserve Bank of India has called chief executive officers of top-tier NBFCs to a meeting today, 23 November, as part of its periodic interaction with the central bank, the Economic Times reported on 20 November (01:32 IST). BusinessToday (21 Nov, updated 16:42 IST) and CNBC-TV18 (22 Nov, 22:10 IST) reported that executives from housing finance companies and microfinance institutions will also attend and that the Governor and all deputy governors are expected present; ET reported that Governor Sanjay Malhotra is most likely to chair, and that these meetings are an annual affair, the last in January 2026.

There is no fixed agenda. ET quotes a senior NBFC executive: "There is no specific agenda for the meeting so far but there could be a central point for the RBI to discuss like customer service was the last time." BusinessToday quotes an industry executive: "There is nothing specific on agenda, but it gives an opportunity to all of us to speak up and share insights and concerns."

The three reports expect cyber risks, higher delinquencies in gold loans, and the impact of a weak monsoon and drought in large agrarian states such as Maharashtra to come up. BusinessToday and CNBC-TV18 reported that MFIs may seek to replace the ₹3 lakh annual household income cap with state-linked thresholds, with the 50% repayment-to-income cap also in play. ET also carries TransUnionCibil figures it published earlier this month: gold-loan NPAs rose to 0.3% at end-August 2026 from 0.16% at end-March; 27% of gold-loan borrowers hold four or more gold loans; and outstanding gold loans reached a record ₹22.5 lakh crore in August 2026, almost three times August 2023.

No agenda has been published and the meeting has not happened at writing time: this report records it as reported and as pending, not as a rule change and not as a decision.
Possible impact on Muthoot Fincorp: no Muthoot Fincorp-specific detail about the meeting appears in the sources checked; the subjects reported as likely are sector-wide, and nothing is predicted here.
Sources: [CNBC-TV18, 22 Nov](https://www.cnbctv18.com/business/finance/rbi-governor-sanjay-malhotra-to-meet-nbfc-mfi-executives-on-november-23-20039436.htm) · [BusinessToday, 21 Nov](https://www.businesstoday.in/latest/economy/story/rbi-to-meet-nbfcs-on-november-23-microfinance-stress-gold-loans-and-cybersecurity-risks-in-focus-568901-2026-11-21) · [Economic Times, 20 Nov](https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/banking/finance/cyber-risks-gold-loans-may-be-top-talking-points-at-rbi-meet/articleshow/136004138.cms)

### Gold rebounds at the Monday Asian open; Friday's settlements stand
Spot gold rose 1.1% to $3,578.24 an ounce at 8:26 a.m. in Singapore — 05:56 IST — on Monday, Bloomberg reported via Moneycontrol (23 Nov, 06:52 IST), after falling 9% last week to a 14-month low; bullion rose as much as 1.3% to around $3,582, and spot silver was up 2.6% at $42.21 after tumbling 15% the week before.

The reported reason, per the same piece: traders scaled back bets on the Federal Reserve raising rates in the near term — swaps traders are no longer fully pricing in a December hike after Treasury yields fell across the curve on Friday, the two-year ending 12 basis points lower; gold has traded below $4,000 since 11 November.

FXStreet's parallel read (23 Nov, 01:09 GMT), quoted with its own attribution rather than averaged: gold around $3,575, markets pricing a 93.2% chance of a 25 basis point Fed hike in December — a different snapshot, not adopted here.

Friday's 20 Nov settlements stand, unchanged and not new today: Comex December gold settled at $3,515.40 (−4.62%) and December silver at $41.07 (−7.41%) (The Edge, 20 Nov); the front-month contract lost $367.40, or 9.47%, for the week to $3,512.30, the largest weekly decline since the week ending 20 March 2026 (Dow Jones Data Talk via Morningstar, 20 Nov 13:53 ET, 18:53 GMT). The rebound is a spot read, not a domestic benchmark: IBJA has posted no 23 Nov rate, so the rupee rows below remain the 20 Nov PM session and today's AGLOC ceiling is set on the 20 Nov reference either way.
Possible impact on Muthoot Fincorp: a higher spot price eases the collateral arithmetic at the margin; no Muthoot Fincorp figure tied to this morning's move appears in the sources checked, and today's ceilings are unchanged — they are the block in the fourth card.
Sources: [Moneycontrol (Bloomberg), 23 Nov](https://www.moneycontrol.com/news/business/commodities/gold-rebounds-as-traders-pare-bets-on-near-term-fed-rate-hikes-14086741.html) · [FXStreet, 23 Nov](https://www.fxstreet.com/news/gold-recovers-above-3-550-as-ai-trade-concern-spurs-safe-haven-flows-202611230109) · [The Edge, 20 Nov settlements](https://edgeconsultancykw.com/commodities-wrap-20-november-2026/) · [Morningstar (Dow Jones), 20 Nov](https://www.morningstar.com/news/dow-jones/202611206877/comex-gold-ends-the-week-947-lower-at-351230-data-talk) · [IBJA](https://ibjarates.com/)

### The policy backdrop the meeting sits in: repo at 5.50%, MPC on 2–4 December, and the industry's asks
The meeting sits six days before the Monetary Policy Committee's next meeting, 2–4 December 2026, decision due 4 December. The policy repo rate stands at 5.50%, raised 25 basis points at the MPC meeting of 5–7 October 2026, with the stance changed to calibrated tightening (RBI home page; October resolution). October CPI inflation was 6.09%, up from 5.54% in September — the first breach of the 6% upper tolerance band in two years — and economists expect 25 basis points in December with a 6.00–6.25% terminal repo (Business Standard, 13 and 16 Nov).

ET reported on 23 Nov that bank executives met top RBI officials last week ahead of the 4 December review, with a 25 or 50 basis point hike being weighed; a person aware of the deliberations said stress is "building up in gold loans which will be felt more by lenders who gave loans close to 85% of loan to value and now need more collateral because gold prices have dropped sharply."

The industry's asks are representations, not changes: through the newly formed Federation of Gold Loan Companies, gold-loan NBFCs have asked RBI to review the minimum Tier-I capital requirement, seeking a cut from 12% to 10%, and the 100% risk weights on gold-loan exposures (Mint, 17 Nov); separately, IIFL Finance has called for gold loans by NBFCs to be brought back under priority-sector lending (Mint, 17 Nov). Muthoot Fincorp chief executive Shaji Varghese, quoted by Mint, questioned why gold-loan companies should face a higher capital threshold, and flagged the continuous LTV requirement and restrictions on rolling over consumer gold loans. No instrument doing any of this appears in the sources checked.
Possible impact on Muthoot Fincorp: its last published capital figure is CRAR 19.38% (14 Nov Q2 filing); the asks concern the Tier-I minimum, a different measure, and remain asks.

### Today's AGLOC block: ₹9,646 / ₹9,078 / ₹8,511, unchanged since Friday evening
AGLOC's published block, verbatim: "Maximum Loan To Value permissible for 23 rd Nov 2026 85% : Rs. 9646 / gm * 80% : Rs. 9078 / gm * 75% : Rs. 8511 / gm * *on Gold Jewellery price of Rs 11348 /-". The block is labelled 23 November, today is 23 November: this is today's block and it applies today, unchanged since it was published on Friday evening. It is internally consistent — 85% of ₹11,348 is ₹9,645.8, published as ₹9,646 — on a reference that equals IBJA's 20 Nov PM 916 rate (₹11,348.6 a gram) rounded down. Against the 20 Nov block — ₹10,085 / ₹9,492 / ₹8,898 on a ₹11,865 reference — today's ceilings are ₹439, ₹414 and ₹387 a gram lower.

The practical point: a ceiling is a rupee figure per gram, so a lower reference lowers what the same pledged gold supports — fresh loans against the same grams are smaller at every band, and loans already written close to a band carry a thinner cushion. This morning's spot rebound does not change the block, which is set on the 20 Nov reference.
Possible impact on Muthoot Fincorp: each gram at the 85% band supports a maximum loan ₹439 smaller than under the 20 Nov block, likewise at every band; the sources checked give no Muthoot Fincorp LTV or loan-book figure for 23 Nov.
Sources: [AGLOC](https://www.agloc.org/) · [IBJA](https://ibjarates.com/)

### ICRA confirms final ratings on the Alpha 2026 merchant-loan PTCs
ICRA on 20 November confirmed as final its ratings on the Alpha 2026 pass-through certificates, backed by unsecured QR-code-based merchant loan receivables originated by Muthoot Fincorp. PTC Series A1, ₹42.13 crore, is [ICRA]AA+(SO); the equity PTC, ₹2.49 crore, is [ICRA]AA-(SO). Muthoot Fincorp is originator and servicer; the pool's aggregate principal outstanding is ₹49.86 crore.

Pool facts: 2,405 obligors, top 10 at 1.2% of pool principal, average seasoning about 4 months, one month post-securitisation. Performance: cumulative collection efficiency 99.40%; loss-cum-0+ dpd 7.81% (unbilled and overdue principal on delinquent contracts, as a share of initial pool principal); 30+ and 90+ dpd both 0.00%. Cash collateral is 5.00% of initial pool principal. Said plainly: a securitisation of the non-gold, unsecured merchant book, performing on collections so far — not a gold-loan transaction, and it says nothing about gold collateral.
Possible impact on Muthoot Fincorp: a rating action dated 20 Nov, not a new filing; today's investor-page check is in the standing facts below.

## 🏘️ Sector Deep Dive — Monday: the funding-cost channel between the repo and a gold lender

Monday has no fixed sector rotation; this is one short read.

The RBI meets NBFC chief executives today, six days before the MPC of 2–4 December, with the repo at 5.50% and economists expecting a 6.00–6.25% terminal (Business Standard, 13 and 16 Nov). For a lender whose FY26 average cost of borrowing was 9.11% and whose bank term loans are 39.69% of borrowings (BusinessLine, 12 Nov), the refixing of deposit and wholesale rates is how a policy rate reaches the P&L — a mechanism, not a forecast: nothing in the sources says what the MPC will do on 4 December.

Q2's asset-quality turn is a repayment-architecture story as much as a price story: LTV is now computed on the amount repayable at maturity, including interest, which is why lenders moved to monthly-interest, shorter-tenor products and why Stage-2 rose even where collateral stayed adequate (CNBC-TV18, 18 Nov). No Muthoot Fincorp LTV, Stage-2, auction or funding-cost figure for November 2026 appears in the sources checked; none is estimated here.

# 📋 NBFC Regulatory Daily Report
**Date:** Monday, 23 November 2026 (IST)

Monday edition for 23 November 2026 (IST), covering Sunday 22 Nov to Monday morning; regulator pages read 07:03–07:35 IST; the exchanges open at 09:15 today, so market figures elsewhere are Friday 20 Nov closes.

---

## 🔔 New Regulatory Updates Today

No new RBI, SEBI or IBBI instrument on 21, 22 or 23 November changes a rule that applies to Muthoot Fincorp. The day's live regulatory event is not an instrument: the RBI meets chief executives of top-tier NBFCs today, as reported by ET, BusinessToday and CNBC-TV18, with no agenda published — an interaction, pending at writing time. What was checked is set out below; the substance is the standing gold-loan rulebook, that meeting, and the next scheduled decision, the MPC on 2–4 December.

### The standing rulebook: RBI (Lending Against Gold and Silver Collateral) Directions, 2025
The Directions were issued on 6 June 2025 (RBI/2025-26/47 DOR.CRE.REC.26/21.01.023/2025-26), updated on 29 September 2025 by the (1st Amendment) Directions (RBI/2025-26/84 DOR.CRE.REC.52/21.01.023/2025-26); compliance was required by 1 April 2026, and loans sanctioned before a lender adopted them stay under the earlier rules. Para 15 caps bullet-repayment consumption loans at 12 months, renewable under para 11; para 16 caps ornaments at 1 kg of gold (10 kg silver) and coins at 50 g gold (500 g silver) per borrower; para 17 values collateral at the lower of the average closing price of that purity over the preceding 30 days and the closing price on the preceding day, per IBJA or a SEBI-regulated commodity exchange; para 19 sets maximum LTV at 85% (loans up to ₹2.5 lakh), 80% (₹2.5–5 lakh) and 75% (above ₹5 lakh); para 20 requires the prescribed LTV to be maintained on an ongoing basis throughout the tenor. Under the revised framework, LTV is computed on the amount repayable at maturity, including interest, for bullet-repayment loans — not merely the amount disbursed.

On auctions: para 37 requires adequate notice to the borrower or legal heir, and one month from the public notice where the borrower cannot be located; para 38 requires advertisements in at least two newspapers, one regional and one national; para 39 puts the auction through the lender's trained employee or an empanelled auctioneer; para 40 sets a reserve price not less than 90% of current value, 85% only after two failed auctions; para 41 requires the first auction physically in the lending branch's district, an adjoining district or online auction only if the first fails; para 42 bars the lender and related parties from bidding; para 43 requires the value fetched and dues adjusted to go to the borrower, any surplus refunded within seven working days of receiving the full proceeds.

Why this rulebook matters today: the subjects reported as likely at the meeting sit directly on it — delinquencies in a book whose LTV is maintained ongoing (para 20) on collateral valued at the lower of a 30-day average and the preceding day's close (para 17), which is why a falling price reaches the books at once and why today's AGLOC ceiling is ₹439 a gram lower at the 85% band than the 20 Nov block. The industry's asks — Tier-I 12% to 10%, a review of the 100% risk weights, PSL inclusion — are representations, not rules; the industry has asked RBI to review, and no instrument doing any of them appears in the sources checked.

Possible impact on Muthoot Fincorp: these are the Directions Muthoot Fincorp's gold-loan book and auction practice run under; nothing in them changed today, and the reported delinquency discussion is a discussion, not an amendment.
Sources: [RBI: Lending Against Gold and Silver Collateral Directions, 2025](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/NotificationUser.aspx?Id=12859) · [RBI: (1st Amendment) Directions, 29 Sep 2025](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/NotificationUser.aspx?Id=12903) · [AGLOC](https://www.agloc.org/) · [Mint, 17 Nov 2026](https://www.livemint.com/industry/banking/gold-loan-nbfcs-seek-rbi-relief-on-capital-norms-as-new-rules-raise-npa-concerns-11794919898824.html)

### The day's regulatory event: RBI meets top-tier NBFC chief executives — an interaction, not an instrument
The RBI has called chief executives of top-tier NBFCs to a meeting today, 23 November, in its periodic interaction with the sector, ET reported (20 Nov); BusinessToday and CNBC-TV18 reported that executives from housing finance companies and microfinance institutions will also attend, and that the Governor and all deputy governors are expected present, with no fixed agenda — annual affairs, the last in January 2026 (ET). The meeting is not a rule change and not an outcome: no agenda has been published, it has not happened at writing time, and nothing is known about what the RBI will say. The subjects reported as likely are the news report's lead story.
Possible impact on Muthoot Fincorp: none to state — no Muthoot Fincorp-specific detail appears in the sources checked; recorded as reported and as pending.
Sources: [CNBC-TV18, 22 Nov 2026, 22:10 IST](https://www.cnbctv18.com/business/finance/rbi-governor-sanjay-malhotra-to-meet-nbfc-mfi-executives-on-november-23-20039436.htm) · [BusinessToday, 21 Nov 2026](https://www.businesstoday.in/latest/economy/story/rbi-to-meet-nbfcs-on-november-23-microfinance-stress-gold-loans-and-cybersecurity-risks-in-focus-568901-2026-11-21) · [Economic Times, 20 Nov 2026](https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/banking/finance/cyber-risks-gold-loans-may-be-top-talking-points-at-rbi-meet/articleshow/136004138.cms)

### The next scheduled decision: the MPC meets 2–4 December
The next Monetary Policy Committee meeting is on 2–4 December 2026, decision due 4 December. The policy repo rate stands at 5.50%, raised 25 basis points at the MPC meeting of 5–7 October 2026, with the stance changed to calibrated tightening (RBI home page; October resolution). October CPI inflation was 6.09%, up from 5.54% in September — the first breach of the 6% upper tolerance band in two years — with food inflation at 8.94% (Business Standard, 13 Nov, recording a 6.00% terminal repo expected by economists — Barclays; a separate 16 Nov report puts the range at 6.00–6.25%, Morgan Stanley and J.P. Morgan at 6.25%). ET's 23 Nov report on the pre-policy consultations — a 25 or 50 basis point hike being weighed, drought and gold-loan stress raised — is the news report's third card. Nothing in the sources says what the MPC will decide on 4 December; this report does not predict it.
Possible impact on Muthoot Fincorp: a scheduled decision, not a change; its last published capital figure — CRAR 19.38% (14 Nov Q2 filing) — stands regardless.

## What was checked

What was checked on 23 November between 07:03 and 07:35 IST, direct from this desk: the RBI press-release page, where the newest date block is Nov 20, 2026 and no release is dated 21, 22 or 23 Nov — the 20 Nov items are the same routine list the 21 and 22 Nov editions carried (conversion and switch of state government securities, a 4-day variable rate repo auction under the LAF for today, the monetary penalty on Fusion Finance Limited, auctions of 91/182/364-day Treasury Bills, the weekly statistical supplement, government stock auction results, the second 3-day variable rate repo result, the FEMA (Export and Import of Goods and Services) (Second Amendment) Regulations, 2026, and the underwriting auction result), all liquidity, debt-management and data operations apart from the one penalty, and none a rule for gold-loan NBFCs — while the page footer reads "Website last updated date: Nov 21, 2026", the site's own stamp, not a release, and today's one dated release (the 4-day VRR, prid=64016) is an operation, not a rule; the RBI notifications feed, latest instrument still the 11 Nov 2026 Domestic Money Transfer Directions, nothing dated 19–23 Nov; SEBI's circular list, latest still the 17 Nov 2026 commodity-derivatives margin framework circular — not NBFC lending — nothing dated 18–23 Nov; and the IBBI site, footer still "Last updated on: 16 Nov 2026", nothing dated 19–23 Nov. The SEBI Credit Risk-o-Meter, in force since 21 November, is therefore out of the deadline list below. Net: no new RBI, SEBI or IBBI instrument on 21, 22 or 23 November changes a rule applying to Muthoot Fincorp, and the day's regulatory event — the NBFC chief executives' meeting — is an interaction the press reports as pending, not an instrument.

cards.title: The standing rulebook: RBI (Lending Against Gold and Silver Collateral) Directions, 2025
cards.summary: The Directions were issued on 6 June 2025 (RBI/2025-26/47 DOR.CRE.REC.26/21.01.023/2025-26), updated on 29 September 2025 by the (1st Amendment) Directions (RBI/2025-26/84 DOR.CRE.REC.52/21.01.023/2025-26); compliance was required by 1 April 2026, and loans sanctioned before a lender adopted them stay under the earlier rules. Para 15 caps bullet-repayment consumption loans at 12 months, renewable under para 11; para 16 caps ornaments at 1 kg of gold (10 kg silver) and coins…
cards.impact: these are the Directions Muthoot Fincorp's gold-loan book and auction practice run under; nothing in them changed today, and the reported delinquency discussion is a discussion, not an amendment.
